headline: South Korean memory maker SK hynix reportedly wants Washington to let more US chipmaking equipment go to its Chinese plant as the price of building a new US factory.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a Reuters exclusive on export-control bargaining, but it rests on unnamed sources and the company disputes it.
importance_line: It affects chip buyers, workers and governments in the US, South Korea and China because US limits on tools for Chinese factories are tight; the account rests on unnamed sources and SK hynix says it is not seeking to expand capacity.
summary: Reuters reports, citing sources, as relayed by TrendForce, that SK hynix wants the US to approve exports of American chipmaking equipment to China as a condition of investing in a new US factory, with its US unit Solidigm planning to add tools to unused space at its Dalian plant in China (which makes NAND flash, the memory used in storage drives) to help fund the US plant. SK hynix told Reuters the Dalian installation is under US government authorisation and that it is not seeking to expand capacity there, and Solidigm declined to comment.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); text read via TrendForce, which credits Reuters. Link is the Reuters original.
